subject: Re: Performance SLO / SLA follow-up - latency measurement & remedies

Subject: Follow-up: performance targets and SLA wording (post-demo)

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and the items I promised to follow up on: 

- Target latency/throughput: your engineering team confirmed a p95 latency target of ~200ms and p99 ~500ms for standard text generation calls (non-streaming). You also mentioned a peak throughput target of ~200 req/s with a concurrency target of ~50 concurrent inferences per region.
- Streaming: you need streaming for the checkout-confirmation flows such that the first token is delivered within ~50ms and subsequent tokens have stable tail latency (important for UX on slow networks).
- Measurement: we discussed measuring latency at Redwood’s edge (ingress) to keep a consistent baseline, excluding the customer network and device rendering. We touched on exclusions — scheduled maintenance windows, customer-triggered misconfigurations, and DDoS/force majeure.
- Reporting & remedies: you asked for monthly reporting and an SLA with service credits for sustained breaches (we said we’ll propose standard language and options).

Next steps from our side:
1) I’ll circulate a short draft of SLA language that captures measurement points, exclusions, reporting cadence, and proposed remedy tiers.
2) Product to confirm feasibility of the streaming-first-token SLA (Rishi), and SRE to confirm how we’ll compute p95/p99 for mixed streaming/non-streaming workloads (Naomi).
3) Legal/Procurement — we’ll flag any non-standard credit caps and escalate if you need higher limits.

Would you also confirm the region(s) you’d like to start with (we recommend us-west + eu-west for compliance reasons) and whether the 200 req/s is steady-state or burst capacity?

I’ve attached a short latency measurement spec and will send a draft SLA shortly.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the summary and for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our infra team: 

- The 200 req/s is our expected steady-state for region us-west during peak business hours; we expect bursts up to ~400 req/s for short periods (up to 15 minutes). If you can support graceful burst handling without client-side failures, that’s preferred.
- For streaming, the 50ms first-token target is what we ideally want for the customer-facing checkout flow. If you can get within 50–100ms that would still be acceptable, we can be flexible on the absolute threshold if there are tradeoffs with cost.
- Measurement: we prefer SLA measurement at the ingress edge as you suggested, but please confirm that your measurement excludes cold-starts for new model instances (we don’t want those to count against you unless they happen frequently).
- Reporting cadence monthly is fine. For remedies, our legal team asked if you can provide a cap in dollar terms or a defined credit schedule instead of open-ended remedies.

Also — can you call out how you compute p95/p99 for composite workflows where a request fans out to multiple Redwood calls (we have a pipeline that does a ranking call followed by a generation call)? Do you aggregate per-call or measure end-to-end user-perceived latency?

Appreciate it — looping in Procurement & Legal for visibility.

Best,
John
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Payments

- Confirm steady-state vs burst handling (200 steady, 400 burst up to 15m) and whether we can provide buffering/graceful degradation strategies (burst queueing, short-lived autoscale).
- Streaming first-token SLA: feasibility and whether we can promise <50ms p95 or whether we should propose p95 <100ms and p50 <50ms. Also call out implementation details (edge TLS termination, push/HTTP/2 chunking impact).
- Measurement exclusions: confirm exclusion for cold starts, scheduled maintenance windows, and customer network issues. Also confirm that for fanned workflows we need to specify whether SLA applies per-call or end-to-end.

Naomi: can you outline how SRE would calculate p95/p99 in the presence of multi-call workflows (rank -> generate) and how we’d surface that in monthly reports?
Rishi: will product/infra accept a client-side recommended pattern for handling bursts (recommended queue depth, retry/backoff config) we can include in the SOW?

I drafted proposed SLA wording (attached) — please review and mark any items that are non-standard. Procurement/Legal from Acme will likely request dollar caps for credits, so think about a standard credit schedule (e.g., 10% credit for single-month breach p99 > 500ms, scaling to higher credits for repeated violations).

Thanks — need your notes by Mon 16th so I can get a clean draft back to John and Procurement.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLO / SLA follow-up - proposed language & next steps

John — thanks for the detail. Per internal reviews (Rishi and Naomi looped), please find our proposed SLA language below and a short note on measurement and remedies. I’ve attached a PDF with the redline-ready draft as well as the latency measurement spec.

Proposed SLA (summary):
- Measurement point: all latency SLOs are measured at Redwood’s ingress edge (post-TLS termination) per-region. This measurement excludes customer network latency and client rendering time.
- Latency thresholds (example): p50 < 50ms (streaming first-token), p95 < 200ms (non-streaming generation), p99 < 500ms (non-streaming generation). For streaming flows we will measure first-token latency separately from tail token throughput; first-token p95 is the key SLA.
- Throughput & concurrency: we will support steady-state 200 req/s and concurrency 50 per-region. Burst handling: we will support transient bursts up to 400 req/s for periods up to 15 minutes. For sustained bursts beyond 15 minutes we will shift to best-effort scaling or negotiated reserved capacity.
- Cold starts & exclusions: cold starts for new model instances (defined as a model instance that has not served at least 5 requests in the previous 10 minutes) are excluded from SLA calculations. Scheduled maintenance windows (>=48 hours notice) and documented customer-side misconfiguration/DNS issues or credential failures are excluded. Major incident events (e.g., DDoS) are excluded when verified by both parties.
- Composite workflows: SLA measurement defaults to per-call SLOs. If the customer requires an end-to-end user-perceived SLA across multiple calls (e.g., rank -> generate), we will define an E2E measurement method in the SOW; this typically requires additional instrumentation and may be scoped as a product/custom-engagement.
- Reporting & remedies: monthly SLO reports delivered to the customer. Service credit schedule (example): single-month breach (p99 > threshold) = 10% service credit on monthly invoice; repeat breach within 3 months = 25% credit; three or more breaches within 12 months = 50% credit and eligibility to discuss termination rights. Total credits are capped at 100% of the monthly invoice. Credits are the exclusive remedy.

Notes: Naomi confirmed we can produce per-region percentile metrics and a monthly report with raw histograms. Rishi confirmed the streaming-first-token target is achievable at p95 <= 100ms across our recommended region setup; promising p95 <50ms is aggressive and depends on customer edge proximity and network conditions — we recommend using p95 <100ms as contractual language with a product-run target of p95 <50ms where feasible.

Next steps:
- Marissa to send attached redline SLA to Procurement/Legal (this email) for review and mark-up.
- John / Acme: confirm whether you want per-call SLAs or an E2E SLA for the checkout flow.
- If Acme wants p95 <50ms first-token contractually, we’ll need to scope reserved capacity and edge placement (additional cost) — Rishi will provide an estimate.

If this looks reasonable I’ll ask Legal to prepare a DocuSign with the option rows (standard credit schedule vs. custom cap) so Procurement can pick.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if your Legal/Procurement teams want to walk through the draft.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
